root_cause.text: The usbtmc driver used usb_bulk_msg() with user-specified timeouts, which performs an unkillable wait, allowing a user to hang a kernel thread indefinitely by providing an arbitrarily large timeout value.
root_cause.evidence: The patch fixes this by replacing usb_bulk_msg() calls with usb_bulk_msg_killable() in three locations within drivers/usb/class/usbtmc.c (usbtmc488_ioctl_trigger, send_request_dev_dep_msg_in, and usbtmc_read). The commit message explicitly states: "Since the user can specify arbitrarily long timeouts and usb_bulk_msg() uses unkillable waits, call usb_bulk_msg_killable() instead to avoid the possibility of the user hanging a kernel thread indefinitely."

intent_record.intent_summary: Make the USBTMC trigger IOCTL operation killable to prevent unkillable process hangs.
intent_record.how: Changes the kernel function used for USB bulk message transfer from uninterruptible to killable, allowing the waiting process to be terminated by a fatal signal (SIGKILL) instead of remaining stuck in an uninterruptible sleep.

intent_record.how: The blocking USB bulk message transmission is now interruptible by fatal signals (e.g., SIGKILL), allowing the waiting process to be terminated instead of hanging indefinitely.
